html:
SMTO-LLM-0006 — Model endpoint name could not be resolved

GUID: 2eca82b4-f9af-4fa6-b5cf-42ba36b752d6
Slug: llm-dns-resolution-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find the model server's computer by the name it was given. The name may be misspelled, or this network may not know it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and check the computer name in Endpoint for typos. One wrong letter means the name can't be found.
  2. If the model server is on a private or work network, make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to it, for example through the VPN. Some names only work inside a particular network.
  3. If it still can't be found, ask your network administrator for the model server's correct name or IP address and enter it in Endpoint, then select Save Main. An exact address lets SMTO reach the server without looking up the name.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model on the Main card passes and a new task gets an answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the model server's name, to your network administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off security checks to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • DNS resolution of the model endpoint's hostname failed (socket.gaierror) before any connection attempt.

What this means

  • The hostname lookup failed before SMTO could use an address for this connection. This does not establish that the model service is stopped or that a dependency is missing. A misspelled hostname, unavailable DNS or a name visible only on another network can cause the same observation.

Why this can happen

  • The hostname may be misspelled or unavailable to the requesting machine’s DNS resolver. A private hostname may require the intended network connection.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the hostname in Model Configuration with the provider address. Test name resolution from the machine issuing the request; success on another machine does not prove this machine can resolve it.

How to fix it

  • Check the hostname in the role's Endpoint field in Settings › Setup › Model routing and test resolution from the Server host (for example getent hosts or nslookup). Correct the name, use an IP address, or restore DNS or VPN access so the Server can resolve it.
  • Check the hostname in Model Configuration and DNS access from the requesting machine. Correct the name or restore the required network connection.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open LLM Endpoint: model-configuration / llm_base_url. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The requesting machine resolves the configured hostname and can then attempt a connection to the intended provider.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Typed transport exception (or exact legacy standard reason where supported); no tool outcome is inferred from connection state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
